top_stories.title: 'NovaCookies' Kit Steals Microsoft 365 Sessions for $320 a Month
top_stories.summary: A phishing-as-a-service kit called "NovaCookies" is being sold for $320 per month, enabling adversary-in-the-middle attacks that steal Microsoft 365 session cookies rather than just credentials. The service bypasses MFA by hijacking authenticated sessions, posing a direct threat to Microsoft 365 identity security.

top_stories.title: NovaCookies Campaigns Abuse Genuine Docusign Notifications to Steal Microsoft 365 Sessions
top_stories.summary: Researchers have disclosed a new adversary-in-the-middle phishing toolkit called NovaCookies, sold as a $320/month subscription service, that proxies Microsoft 365 sign-ins to steal authenticated session cookies. The attack abuses legitimate DocuSign notifications to bypass MFA by capturing post-authentication sessions rather than credentials directly.

top_stories.title: Okta’s AI boom just created a new security problem
top_stories.summary: Okta reported fiscal Q2 revenue of $805 million (up 11%), with subscription revenue reaching $793 million, while highlighting a new security challenge posed by AI "workers" requiring identity management. The article addresses how the rise of AI agents is creating new identity and access management concerns that extend beyond traditional human user authentication.

top_stories.title: Key Reasons Why Identity Fabric Matters in 2026
top_stories.summary: This article explains the concept of Identity Fabric architecture and its relevance to enterprise identity security in 2026. It covers how Identity Fabric integrates fragmented identity systems to provide runtime visibility across cloud services, APIs, and automated workloads, and addresses risks associated with unmanaged identities.

news.title: Okta Just Jumped 29%. AI Agents May Be Creating a New Bottleneck
news.summary: Okta's stock jumped 28.6% on August 27, closing at $172.91 after reporting better-than-expected earnings results and reaching a four-year high. The article discusses how AI agents may be creating new identity and access management bottlenecks, framing Okta's growth in the context of expanding demand for machine identity management.

news.title: CrowdStrike and Okta Soar as AI Could Create “About 90” New Identities Per Worker
news.summary: CrowdStrike and Okta stocks rose amid predictions that AI could generate approximately 90 new identities per worker, significantly expanding the identity management landscape. The projection highlights growing demand for IAM and cybersecurity solutions as AI agents and automated systems require their own managed identities.

news.title: A Deadline No One Can Negotiate Is Coming for the World’s Encryption, and the Race to Get Ready Has Quietly Begun
news.summary: Quantum Secure Encryption Corp issued commentary on the approaching threat of quantum computing to current encryption standards, including those protecting identity and authentication systems. The piece addresses the urgency of transitioning to post-quantum cryptography across sectors including banking, identity, and government records.

news.title: CrowdStrike and Okta shares soar as AI threats fuel cybersecurity spending
news.summary: CrowdStrike and Okta shares rose sharply after both companies beat quarterly earnings estimates and raised forecasts, with Okta's stock climbing significantly. The results were attributed to increased cybersecurity spending driven by AI-related threats.

news.title: AI IR Overlay – Incident Response Specification for AI Agents
news.summary: A specification called AI IR Overlay has been published addressing incident response procedures for AI agents, including containment protocols for agents operating with valid credentials. The specification includes a kill-switch contract mechanism but acknowledges a gap in coverage when no SOC is staffed.

news.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
news.summary: Canadian cybercriminal Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy charges related to hacking and extorting over 165 organizations using Snowflake cloud storage. The attacks involved unauthorized access to Snowflake accounts, largely exploiting stolen credentials and the absence of MFA enforcement.

news.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
news.summary: CISA released a postmortem on a data breach in which a contractor accidentally published dozens of internal CISA credentials, including AWS GovCloud keys, to a public GitHub repository for nearly six months. The incident highlights credential management and secrets management failures, with security experts drawing lessons for security teams around detecting and responding to exposed credentials.
